scorecard.rationale: The independent red grape seed-extract Parkinson rat comparison reports lower cumulative muscle stiffness scores versus both untreated and vehicle lesion controls. The effect has a focused rigidity readout, while the exposure is a hydroalcoholic seed extract and the model differs from human Parkinson disease. The new isolated-resveratrol mouse study improved open-field movement and rotarod retention without a separate rigidity measurement. The earlier red grape juice comparison reported drug-induced turns without a verified juice-versus-lesion contrast, and the clinical juice-plus-exercise report used baseline motor scores. The original seed-extract signal retains minimal easing for the frozen grape hypothesis. No whole frozen fruit and clinical rigidity comparison is verified.
